patients.label: 61-year-old woman with EGPA and steroid-refractory eosinophilic otitis media treated with alternating tezepelumab and mepolizumab

identity_evidence.quote: We report a case of steroid-refractory eosinophilic otitis media (EOM) in a patient with EGPA

attribution_limitations: Literal source conflict on age: the disease had become refractory at age 61, prednisolone was increased to 15 mg/day without sufficient benefit, and "Given the insufficient clinical response" tezepelumab was started, yet the start is stated at age 60. Both age-bearing sides are quarantined (source_conflict, review_only) on their age/time; the referral age of 61 is not a side because its order relative to tezepelumab is not stated.

The sentence on tezepelumab-related improvement (asthma symptoms, nasal obstruction, FeNO 46 to 19 ppb, EOM) carries citations to a published trial and to an earlier case report by the same author group. Reviewer ruling: the sentence is about this patient ("This upstream TSLP inhibitor" refers back to the tezepelumab started in this patient and the FeNO values are individual measurements); the citations support the general claim. Facts are kept as patient facts.

Figure 1 pixel content shows peripheral eosinophil values rising to roughly 155/μl at X+3 and about 110-125/μl at several later points after tezepelumab was introduced, while the text says serial peripheral eosinophil counts remained suppressed during the alternating regimen. Plotted values are pixel content only and are not a conflict side.

The abstract describes a bi-monthly alternating regimen, while the body text says tezepelumab and mepolizumab were alternated monthly with each agent given every other month. The two wordings are compatible but not identical.

Audiometry before alternating therapy is stated for the left ear as three-frequency averages (air 61.7 dB, bone 66.7 dB), whereas the post-treatment sentence gives air conduction 41.7 dB and bone conduction 51.7 dB without restating ear or averaging; the text elsewhere reports improvement in left-ear air conduction. The baseline bone conduction average is printed higher than the air conduction average.

The recurrence of asthma and EOM at which blood eosinophils were 300/μl, the EOM worsening at age 53 and the worsening at which mepolizumab was started at age 56 are described separately; the source does not say whether any of these are the same episode.

Swimlane-style timeline illustrating the clinical course and treatment transitions in a patient with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) and eosinophilic otitis media (EOM). The figure displays the temporal relationship between clinical events, oral prednisolone (PSL) dosing, peripheral eosinophil counts, and the administration of biologics (mepolizumab and tezepelumab). The timeline begins with the initiation of biologic therapy and highlights the lack of sustained control with mepolizumab monotherapy, followed by the introduction of tezepelumab and the subsequent alternation of the two agents at four-week intervals. caption_claims.text:
Figure 1
Swimlane-style timeline illustrating the clinical course and treatment transitions in a patient with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) and eosinophilic otitis media (EOM). The figure displays the temporal relationship between clinical events, oral prednisolone (PSL) dosing, peripheral eosinophil counts, and the administration of biologics (mepolizumab and tezepelumab). The timeline begins with the initiation of biologic therapy and highlights the lack of sustained control with mepolizumab monotherapy, followed by the introduction of tezepelumab and the subsequent alternation of the two agents at four-week intervals. Steroid bursts and clinical relapses are also indicated, providing a visual summary of disease activity and therapeutic response.
